iut_type: End Product (Ricoh Imaging camera), USB Power Delivery Source current threshold
customer_question: For PD compliance, is 900mA the minimum required Source current, or would 500mA be sufficient?
question_variants: Can our product satisfy PD certification requirements with only a 500mA Source current?
What is the actual minimum Source current threshold for PD/DRP eligibility?
actual_issue: The customer's product design was being evaluated against a candidate Source output current of 500mA, and they needed to know whether this met the minimum threshold for PD compliance and DRP (dual-role power) eligibility, or whether a higher current was required.
plain_english_explanation: 500mA is not sufficient — the minimum required Source current for PD compliance is 900mA. A product with a Source output below this threshold cannot qualify for DRP (dual-role power) certification, which has downstream implications for whether the product can be certified as a UFP/DFP dual-role device versus a sink-only (UFP-only) device.
consultant_answer: 500mA is not enough — the minimum required Source current for PD compliance is 900mA. Below that threshold, your product cannot qualify for DRP certification.
decision_logic: PD/DRP certification eligibility is gated on a minimum Source output current threshold (900mA); a lower candidate current (such as 500mA) disqualifies the product from DRP certification regardless of other specification details, and this threshold should be checked early in the hardware design process before committing to a certification path.
final_recommendation: Confirm a product's planned Source output current against the 900mA PD/DRP minimum threshold as early as possible in hardware design, since falling short forecloses DRP certification and forces a fallback to sink-only (UFP-only) certification paths with their own separate constraints.
risk_if_done_wrong: Designing hardware around a 500mA Source assumption would result in late discovery that DRP certification is unavailable, potentially requiring a hardware redesign or a fallback to a more limited certification scope after significant design work is already complete.
